stem:
A pharmaceutical company finds that its new water-soluble antibiotic reaches high concentrations in most tissues but barely enters the cerebrospinal fluid of healthy 40-year-old volunteers.

Which of the following features of brain capillaries most accounts for this exclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: Astrocytes actively importing the drug before it can diffuse
options.misconception: Supporting glia are being cast as a sink that sequesters solutes.
options.explanation: Astrocyte end feet help maintain the barrier but do not consume circulating drugs; exclusion is due to tight junctions and absent vesicular transport in the endothelium.

options.label: B
options.text: Widely fenestrated endothelium that filters proteins into the tissue
options.misconception: The leaky capillary design of other organs is being ascribed to the brain.
options.explanation: Fenestrations characterize permeable capillaries such as those of the kidney; cranial capillaries specifically lack them, which is the basis of the barrier.

options.label: C
options.text: Ependymal cells filtering the blood into cerebrospinal fluid selectively
options.misconception: The CSF-producing epithelium is being treated as the vascular gatekeeper.
options.explanation: Ependymal cells of the choroid plexus produce CSF, but the vascular barrier itself lies in the capillary endothelium's tight junctions; water-soluble drugs are blocked at the vessel wall.

options.label: D
options.text: Tight junctions between endothelial cells, with few pores or transport vesicles
options.misconception: None; the barrier is an anatomical sealing of the capillary wall.
options.explanation: Brain capillary endothelial cells are joined by tight junctions and have far fewer fenestra and pinocytotic vesicles than other capillaries, so water-soluble compounds cannot slip between or through the cells; the barrier preferentially blocks non-lipid-soluble drugs.

options.label: E
options.text: Abundant pinocytotic vesicles that return the drug to the plasma
options.misconception: A transport mechanism that is actually scarce in brain capillaries is being invoked.
options.explanation: Cranial capillaries have far fewer pinocytotic vesicles than other capillaries; their scarcity, together with tight junctions, prevents transcellular passage of polar compounds.

context: Learning objective: explain the blood-brain barrier. Endothelial tight junctions plus scarce fenestra and pinocytotic vesicles seal brain capillaries, excluding water-soluble compounds and admitting lipid-soluble ones.
